correctness.rationale: For 0<=t<=t*, strict t*<lambda_min(A) ensures uniform SPD. The spectral K-bound is equivalently all orthonormal-pair Rayleigh gaps <=0. Exact Frobenius duality turns their worst-case gap into 1-K+t times a two-plane norm; rotation within the compressed plane gives a convex quadratic in squared cosine, maximized at its top H eigenvector, and Ritz interlacing yields the sharp maximum sqrt(K^2/lambda_1^2+1/lambda_2^2). A rank-two commuting unit-Frobenius E realizes equality and scaled copies violate the cap at any larger t. Exact rational two-dimensional calculation and 8472 replayed seeded checks confirm examples; no numerical test substitutes for the proof.

originality.rationale: The claim is the exact finite Frobenius perturbation radius for a uniform spectral-condition-number cap after full spectral whitening of a reference SPD matrix. The inspected 2026 paper has fixed-direction asymptotic PCG versus deflated-CG error inequalities and itself identifies uniform varying-E bounds as a further issue. The March 2026 precursor optimizes finite-iteration energy error for unperturbed systems. Giraud--Gratton (2006) studies derivative-level eigenspectrum sensitivity from inexact eigenelements, not a finite all-directions condition cap. Rump (2003) addresses distance to singularity and condition numbers of matrix inversion. Published-findings searches returned neighboring preconditioning robustness results but not an implication covering the two-smallest-eigenvalues formula with commuting rank-two optimizer.
residual_risks: An older theorem on weighted Frobenius distance to a prescribed condition-number variety could imply the exact formula under a different terminology; no exhaustive priority certification is claimed.
Full whitening is an expensive benchmark; the theorem makes no partial-spectral-preconditioner performance claim.

value.rationale: The sharp radius is a motivated robust-use tolerance for spectral information reused after an unknown symmetric change of a reference SPD system. Compared with the elementary Weyl condition bound lambda_1(K-1)/(K+1), the new radius is strictly larger, depends precisely on two smallest reference eigenvalues independent of dimension, and reveals that a commuting rank-two adversary controls the worst-case noncommuting Frobenius ball. It includes repeated eigenvalues and supplies an exact benchmark for studying more practical partial preconditioners without falsely asserting such an extension.
